input: Pricing case for a SaaS tier. The tier is priced at $51 per unit. Variable cost is $25 per unit, and fixed costs are $139k per year. Break-even volume is 5346 units per year; current volume is 2464 units per year. At the current volume the tier sells below break-even, so the margin on the units sold does not meet the fixed costs of the year. The margin on each unit is the price less the variable cost, and break-even volume is the fixed costs divided by that margin; the stated break-even volume follows from the three figures above, and a reader can check it from them. Current volume is under half the break-even volume, so the gap is not marginal: volume would have to more than double at unchanged price and costs before the tier covered its fixed costs. The volume figures are last year's actuals. The effect of the price on volume is not estimated. The case therefore holds volume at the recorded level: it states the volume the tier must reach at the current price and costs, and it does not state what volume a different price would bring, or whether the market for the tier would take the break-even volume at this price. A decision to hold or change the price takes that open term as it stands; the arithmetic of the case is complete on its own figures, and its limit is the unmodelled response of volume to price, which no restatement of the cost figures can remove.
